AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 15, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  III.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54957(b)(1); TITLE: CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  IV.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE APPOINTMENT PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54957(b)(1);
  TITLE: CITY ATTORNEY.

  V.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Hector Gomez
  New Branch Ministries

FLAG SALUTE
  Leah Mendez, 5th grade
  Paddison Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  Mayor’s Award to Probation Officer Martha Marin-Corbett & Lakeside Middle School Assistant Principal
  Rosa Alcala for their actions in helping rescue a child in distress.

  II.  City Council to proclaim October 13, 2019 as Lions Club White Cane Day in the City of Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to proclaim October 23 - 31, 2019 as Red Ribbon Week in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Housing Summit

  2.  City’s Key to Ending Homelessness
   3.  Sound the Alarm

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  September 30 and October 1, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period September 8, 2019 –
  September 21, 2019, in the total amount of $951,371.58. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  September 25, 2019 – October 8, 2019, in the total amount of $2,356,384.11. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Rosa Marroquin.
  830-13

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – OCTOBER 9, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY REPAIR WORK – FOSTER ROAD AND DALWOOD AVENUE - Staff
  recommends City Council confirm emergency repair work at Foster Road and Dalwood Avenue
  completed by Steven Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc., in the amount of $6,891.11. 955

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-59 - REPORTING OF THE EMPLOYER’S CONTRIBUTION FOR
  MANAGEMENT UNIT EMPLOYEES UNDER THE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL
  CARE ACT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-59, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK RESCINDING RESOLUTION NO. 18-60, AND FIXING
  THE EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTION AT AN EQUAL AMOUNT FOR EMPLOYEES AND ANNUITANTS
  UNDER THE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL CARE ACT FOR MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEES.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  9.  ORDINANCE NO. 19-1708 - AMENDING CHAPTER 15.32 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE
  REGARDING REGULATIONS APPLICABLE TO BUILDINGS AND CONSTRUCTION AND
  MODIFYING THE FILING DATE FOR APPEALS AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-62 - AMENDING THE
   COMPREHENSIVE FEE SCHEDULE TO ESTABLISH FEES FOR CODE ENFORCEMENT CASE
  APPEALS - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 19-1708, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 15.32 ADDING LANGUAGE REGARDING
  A NEW CODE COMPLIANCE APPEAL FEE AND MODIFYING THE FILING DATE FOR
  APPEALS TO CITY COUNCIL, by title only and waive further reading; and

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 19-62, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING THE COMPREHENSIVE FEE SCHEDULE TO ESTABLISH FEES FOR
  CODE ENFORCEMENT CASE APPEALS TO CITY COUNCIL. 305-03/602-01

  Report

RESOLUTIONS

  10. GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - MARCH 3, 2020 - RESOLUTION NOS. 19-63 - CALLING
  ELECTION, 19-64 - CONSOLIDATION WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGISTRAR-RECORDER,
  AND 19-65 - BUDGET AMENDMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-63, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  CALIFORNIA, CALLING FOR THE HOLDING OF A GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE
  HELD ON MARCH 3, 2020, FOR THE ELECTION OF CERTAIN OFFICERS AS REQUIRED BY
  THE PROVISIONS OF THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA RELATING TO GENERAL
  LAW CITIES;

  b.  Resolution No. 19-64, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  CALIFORNIA, REQUESTING THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF THE COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES TO CONSOLIDATE THE CITY OF NORWALK’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION
  TO BE HELD ON TUESDAY, MARCH 3, 2020 WITH THE STATEWIDE PRIMARY ELECTION TO
  BE HELD ON THE DATE PURSUANT TO §10403 OF THE ELECTIONS CODE; and

  c.  Resolution No. 19-65, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR THE MARCH 3, 2020 GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION, in the amount of $153,000. 610/845-03

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 19-66 – AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20
  ADOPTED BUDGET FOR THE PURCHASE OF CAPITAL EQUIPMENT - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 19-66, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED BUDGET
  FOR THE PURCHASE OF CAPITAL EQUIPMENT, in an amount not to exceed $65,000. 610/634-06

  Report

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 19-58 – INITIATING PROCEEDINGS TO VACATE A PORTION OF FORMER
  FIRESTONE BOULEVARD RIGHT-OF-WAY LOCATED ADJACENT TO THE FIRESTONE
  BOULEVARD CUL-DE-SAC SOUTH OF ROSECRANS AVENUE - Staff recommends City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 19-58, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  CALIFORNIA INITIATING PROCEEDINGS TO VACATE A PORTION OF FORMER FIRESTONE
  BOULEVARD RIGHT-OF-WAY LOCATED ADJACENT TO THE FIRESTONE BOULEVARD CUL-DE-
  SAC SOUTH OF ROSECRANS AVENUE, SETTING THE PUBLIC HEARING ON NOVEMBER 19,
  2019, AND DEDICATING THIS CITY OWNED PROPERTY FOR OTHER CITY PURPOSES. 1045-08-
  89

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 19-67 - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 SALARY SCHEDULE - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt RESOLUTION NO. 19-67, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20
  FOR THE GENERAL, HOURLY, AND MANAGEMENT UNIT EMPLOYEES. 135-03
   Report

REPORTS

  14. CITY’S FLEET REPLACEMENT AND MAINTENANCE - Staff recommends City Council approve
  replacing the City’s light-duty vehicles through leasing mechanism; and entering into an agreement
  with Enterprise Fleet Maintenance Inc., for open-end lease of twenty light-duty vehicles, and
  maintenance of the leased vehicles; and authorize the City Manager to execute the master agreement,
  and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney.

  Report

  15. APPROVE CONCEPT DESIGN FOR HERMOSILLO PARK - Staff recommends City Council approve
  the concept design for Hermosillo Park.

  Report

  16. ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PLAN IMPLEMENTATION UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council
  direct staff to update the Economic Development Opportunities Plan.

  Report

  17. COMMUNITY SURVEY RESULTS – Staff is providing this information for City Council discussion and
  consideration.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 11, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
